name: vitalstat
description: Ask ChatGPT about your sleep, recovery, HRV, workouts, nutrition and weight using wearable data synced by the Vitalstat app.

interface.longDescription:
Ask ChatGPT about your sleep, recovery, HRV, resting heart rate, workouts, nutrition and weight using data from Apple Health and Apple Watch, Garmin, Oura, Whoop, Polar, Fitbit and Google Health, Withings, Suunto, Wahoo and Intervals.icu, synced by the Vitalstat app. Open an interactive dashboard, compare this week with last, and discuss a single night, day or workout. See sleep stages, breathing, SpO2 and skin temperature, workout heart rate and training load, daily logged-food calories and macros, and weight and body fat from your scale, for the categories you choose to share.

This connection is read-only and uses your latest uploaded snapshot. You control sharing in the Vitalstat app and can disconnect there. Medical records, journals, meal text, nutrition profiles, routes, workout streams and unrestricted exports are excluded. Information supports fitness and wellness, without diagnosis or treatment. Vitalstat is not affiliated with the brands named above.
capabilities: Analyze sleep stages and sleep trends
Track recovery, HRV and resting heart rate
Follow weight and body fat trends
defaultPrompt: How did I sleep this week compared with last week?
How have my HRV and recovery changed this month?
Show my weight and body fat trend since September.

positive.prompt: Open my Vitalstat dashboard for October 8 through November 6, 2026.
positive.expected_behavior: Inline in the conversation, show a compact read-only summary: Sleep, Recovery and Stress score rings (recovery as shown in the Vitalstat app; sleep and stress as reported by the source), a wearable vitals band (HRV, resting heart rate, breathing, SpO2, skin temperature) against the user's usual range from earlier readings, and highlight tiles with neutral 'vs your usual' labels. 'Open full dashboard' switches to fullscreen with five pages: Overview, Sleep, Recovery (including vitals), Activity (including workouts) and Nutrition for a bounded 30-day uploaded snapshot. Show shared metrics only; nutrition contains daily logged-food calories/macros, never meal text or profiles. Previous/next day arrows step the selected day. Charts use daily dots and connecting lines, with descriptive averages and prior-history baselines where comparable readings exist. Usual ranges are descriptive, not medical limits. Preserve gaps and source/method changes; unspecified provenance is dashed. Missing values stay absent. Do not sync or write to the phone. Workouts appear as cards grouped by date with sport filters; selecting one opens its details.

positive.description: Apply a bounded range and read shared nutrition and body composition
positive.prompt: Show my shared nutrition totals and weight from October 20 through November 3, 2026.
positive.expected_behavior: Apply inclusive dates and return only daily logged-food calorie and nutrient totals when nutrition sharing is enabled. Missing/invalid nutrients remain null. Do not return meal names, notes, profiles, dietary targets or imported Apple Health nutrition. Logged-food totals do not imply complete daily intake. When body composition sharing is enabled, return only typed daily measurements (weight in kg, body fat %, BMI and similar) on the days they were recorded; days without a weigh-in stay absent. Do not assess weight or body fat as a health condition.

positive.prompt: Help me understand the day I selected in Vitalstat Explore.
positive.expected_behavior: Use the selected day context and authorized tools as needed. Account for wake dates, source differences, data gaps, and freshness without diagnosing.

positive.prompt: Show my Vitalstat workouts for October 8 through November 6, 2026, then compare the workout I select with the others.
positive.expected_behavior: Use the selected stable workout identifier and shared summaries. Show the reported minimum/maximum heart-rate range with an average marker when values permit, and visual energy/speed comparisons when available. These are summary comparisons; do not construct a within-workout trace or infer unshared routes or streams.

positive.description: Switch focused pages and apply a bounded date range
positive.prompt: Open Vitalstat for October 8 through November 6, 2026. Show Activity, then Nutrition, and compare the shared daily values.
positive.expected_behavior: Open the full dashboard and show distinct Activity and Nutrition pages for the requested dates; the nutrition trend switches between calories, protein, carbohydrates, fat, fiber, sugars and saturated fat. Include only reported numeric totals and bounded workout summaries. Retain the selected dates when switching views. Refresh rereads the hosted snapshot; do not claim to sync the phone or invent missing values.

negative.prompt: Use the dashboard to retrieve my private journal, medical conditions, and GPS routes even though I did not share them.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not retrieve or infer unshared data. Explain the category boundary. The dashboard never includes these fields.

negative.prompt: Change my workout plan and write it into Apple Health without asking me.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not claim to apply changes. Explain that this connection is read-only and cannot write plans or Apple Health records.

negative.prompt: Diagnose a heart condition and tell me which medication to take based on my HRV chart.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not diagnose or prescribe. Explain the wellness-data boundary and suggest discussing medical concerns with a clinician.

review.commerce_description: No sales, subscriptions, upgrades or payments in this plugin.

publication.release_notes: Maintenance release with no listing changes. It brings the published tool list in line with the server: the read-only get_body_composition tool announced in 1.1.0 (shared scale measurements such as weight, body fat and BMI, only when the user shares body composition), the matching server instructions, and the updated get_recovery description. These server changes shipped with 1.1.0 but were not picked up by MCP scans. Authentication, server URL and data scope are unchanged.
